newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand ended above 4.70 on the dollar on Friday on the back of late demand for the U.S. unit out of London and concern over comments by Finance Minister Trevor Manuel that a committee would be set up to investigate forward cover.
The rand ended the day at 4.7020/7060 on a weaker dollar from 4.7025/7075 at the Thursday close.
"The rand benefited in the morning from a better- than-expected October reserves figure and good dollar selling from offshore," a senior trader said.
October reserves, released late on Thursday, came in at 10.28 billion rand, up from 10.04 billion in September, and compared with a consensus forecast 9.6 billion rand.

The rand was largely unperturbed by comments from Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals that dismantling foreign exchange controls would likely take four to five years and a one-off of "big bang" scrapping of controls was not on the cards.
But it was ruffled by indications on Friday that the government might accelerate the Reserve Bank's withdrawal from the forward foreign exchange market.

Finance Minister Trevor Manuel told a conference he had appointed a committee of Reserve Bank and finance department officials to investigate the provision of forward cover in the foreign exchange market, in view of heavy losses this year.
"Manuel's comments put some pressure on the market...in the longer-term forward cover is an issue," a forex trader said.

Traders said overall market sentiment was fairly neutral with some optimistic that the rand could test the lower 4.65 levels at the start of the week while others believed it would trade above 4.71 on the dollar.
The rand was last trading at 7.7390/7520 against sterling and at 0.3206/3210 against the mark.
Long bond yields ended steady after a stronger start on the back of a better-than-expected October reserves figure and a sharp drop in U.S. rates.
At 1425 GMT the yield on government's benchmark R150 bond was trading at 15.83 percent from 15.85 percent at the local close on Thursday.
"The market started stronger but yields then lingered around the lower 15.80's level in thin, apathetic trade," a bond dealer said.
He said trade had been hampered by a local gilts lunch and players wanting to "take a breather" after a hectic trading day on Thursday which marked the week's bond options close-out.
Dealers expected the market to open up around the 15.81 percent level on Monday with all eyes on the rand to provide near-term direction.
No major economic indicators are scheduled for release next week.

The Bond Exchange said foreigners bought 180.39 million rand of South African bonds on Thursday after buying 242.84 million rand on Wednesday. Nominal cumulative volumes stood at 48.25 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement date -- from 9.29 billion rand on Wednesday.
On the money market, three-month NCD rates were steady at between 16.75 to 16.90 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at between 16.10 to 16.25 percent.
The Reserve Bank indicated the daily shortage slightly lower at 8.661 billion rand on Thursday from 8.829 billion rand on Wednesday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
